To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
‘REDD+ emissions estimation and reporting: the need for conservative estimates to deal with uncertainty’.

(1) the matrix approach can be a valuable tool for uncertainty analysis in REDD+; (2) modelling sources of uncertainty are the most important sources of uncertainty; (3) the adoption of strict reporting rules would favour comparability; (4) a reduction of the uncertainty of emission factors is needed to improve the accuracy and credibility of emission reductions; (5) public access to datasets and methodologies used to evaluate reference emission levels and emission reductions will strengthen the credibility of REDD+ and
‘the matrix approach to REDD+ uncertainty analysis is a useful and robust tool to identify the most sensitive parameters and to assess uncertainty in emission estimates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the need to develop a robust and reliable REDD+ system that is capable of providing the necessary information to make informed decisions and to support the development of a robust REDD+ mechanism.
the need for a robust and reliable system that can be applied in developing countries and which can ensure environmental integrity and transparency.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current technical and financial arrangements for REDD+ in the UNFCCC do not provide the necessary safeguards to ensure the environmental integrity of emission reduction commitments.

the uncertainty in emission factors and in the activity data are the main sources of error and that the uncertainty associated with these sources is the highest in the case of the matrix approach, but that the uncertainty associated to the modelling sources is higher than the uncertainty associated to these sources.

, although there is a high degree of uncertainty in emission estimates, it is possible to estimate forest-related emissions and reductions with a high level of precision and accuracy, which is sufficient to support the development of REDD+.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the REDD+ mechanism is a very complex and challenging process that needs to be carefully designed and implemented to achieve environmental integrity, and that the current state of the art is insufficient to meet the requirements for a robust and reliable system.
REDD+ incentives are not only needed to compensate for the opportunity costs of conservation but also for the costs associated with the uncertainty of the estimates.
the matrix approach proposed is an efficient tool for estimating and reporting uncertainty of REDD+ results.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a REDD+ incentives system that does not consider uncertainty in emissions and removals estimates would not be credible, and that the use of a dashboard of indicators would be a better approach to assess REDD+ results.
the REDD+ framework should be improved by adopting strict rules for estimation, reporting and verification to secure environmental integrity and to avoid double counting of emission reductions.

the REDD+ system needs to be designed in a way that it is flexible enough to accommodate the uncertainties associated with the estimation of forest-related emission reductions, and that the system needs to be designed with the goal of improving the quality and accuracy of estimates over time.
